scope_statement: External duplication boundary for Fermat shell coordinates, multiplier near-square residuals, modular residue filtering, and the finite-window normalized residual-priority multiplier score e_k/(2*x_k-1).
search_surfaces: Cambridge Core / Warwick WRAP (Hart 2012 primary article and published PDF)
AMS / JSTOR / Mathematics of Computation metadata and references (Lehman 1974; McKee 1999)
FLINT public source repository pinned at commit 7c8c3c8f1c134fa93f3af98f044f9958b9c09a72
DOAJ / Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy (Overmars-Venkatraman 2024)
Broad web/literature search for normalized next-square residual ordering and equivalent formulas

Lehman Factoring Large Integers 1974 multiplier 4kn Fermat
Hart A One Line Factoring Algorithm multiplier residual ordering
McKee Speeding Fermat's factoring method modular residue
"distance to next square" multiplier factorization kN
continued fractions one line factoring multiplier selection

sources.citation: William B. Hart, A One Line Factoring Algorithm, Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 92 (2012), 61-69.
findings: OLF is explicitly a Fermat variant.
The algorithm advances multiplier i sequentially and tests the near-square residual from ceil(sqrt(n*i)).
A practical fixed multiplier M=480 and modular square rejection are described.
Hart explicitly relates OLF to Lehman's multiplier-Fermat search.

sources.citation: R. Sherman Lehman, Factoring Large Integers, Mathematics of Computation 28 (1974), 637-646.
findings: Systematizes a modification of Fermat based on multiples of N.
Uses difference-of-squares search on 4*k*N in the classical O(N^(1/3)) framework.
Therefore x_k^2-4*k*N is not a new search object.

sources.citation: Markus Hittmeir, A time-space tradeoff for Lehman's deterministic integer factorization method, Mathematics of Computation 90 (2021), 1999-2010.
findings: Records the historical chain Fermat -> Lawrence (1895 multiples kN) -> Lehman (1974 systematic k).
Confirms multiplier selection is a long-established axis of improvement.

sources.citation: Markus Hittmeir, Integer factorization as subset-sum problem, Journal of Number Theory 249 (2023), 93-118.
findings: Develops a hyperbolic modular sieve and applies it to improve Fermat factorization.
Shows modular elimination/selective search around Fermat remains active prior art.
Does not, in the audited text, order Hart/Lehman multipliers by e/(2*x-1).

sources.citation: James McKee, Speeding Fermat's Factoring Method, Mathematics of Computation 68 (1999), 1729-1737.
findings: Provides a distinct Fermat acceleration using rational-square structure and divisibility constraints.
Relevant as adjacent Fermat optimization, not an exact match for normalized residual-priority multiplier ordering.
Defines FLINT_ONE_LINE_MULTIPLIER=480.
Forms successive in values by in += n after n has been multiplied by 480.
Tests square - in for squareness; it does not compute or sort by normalized residual e/(2*x-1).

sources.citation: Anthony Overmars and Sitalakshmi Venkatraman, Continued Fractions Applied to the One Line Factoring Algorithm for Breaking RSA, Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy 4 (2024), 41-54.
findings: Explores a different k-selection mechanism for OLF via continued-fraction convergents.
Demonstrates that multiplier selection itself is an active research degree of freedom.
No exact normalized next-square residual ordering match was found.

claim_classification.label: EXACT_DUPLICATE
claim_classification.boundary: Coordinate rewrite of classical Fermat difference-of-squares; no novelty inference.

claim_classification.claim: Reject t when Fermat residual is not a quadratic residue modulo chosen moduli.
claim_classification.label: EXACT_DUPLICATE
claim_classification.boundary: Modular square rejection/sieving is established prior art; parent use is a baseline implementation choice.

claim_classification.claim: x_k=ceil(sqrt(4*k*N)), e_k=x_k^2-4*k*N; square e_k yields a difference-of-squares factorization.
claim_classification.label: EXACT_DUPLICATE
claim_classification.boundary: Same multiplier-Fermat/Lehman/Hart near-square object up to conventional multiplier/scaling notation.

claim_classification.claim: Cycle through multipliers and test each near-square residual.
claim_classification.label: EXACT_DUPLICATE
claim_classification.boundary: Hart and FLINT implement sequential multiplier cycling; this is the correct classical baseline.

claim_classification.claim: For a finite k-window, prioritize multipliers by score(k)=e_k/(2*x_k-1), smallest first.
claim_classification.label: NO_MATERIAL_MATCH_IN_AUDITED_SET
claim_classification.boundary: No audited primary/authoritative source was found that uses this exact normalized next-square residual as a factor-blind multiplier ordering. This is NOT a novelty claim; it is only a negative search result over the frozen audit set.

claim_classification.claim: Use information other than ascending k to select/prioritize multipliers.
claim_classification.label: ADJACENT_METHOD
claim_classification.boundary: The broad idea of smarter multiplier selection is old/active; any value of C5 must come from the exact score and proven/empirical performance, not from the generic concept of reordering k.

claim_classification.claim: Improve Fermat search by arithmetic/sieving structure not equivalent to residual-priority.
claim_classification.label: ADJACENT_METHOD
claim_classification.boundary: Strong adjacent prior art; does not duplicate C5 but narrows any possible novelty framing.

normalization_lemma.setup: Let z=4*k*N be nonsquare, x=ceil(sqrt(z)), e=x^2-z and d=x-sqrt(z).
normalization_lemma.interpretation: The score is the exact upper-square gap normalized by the adjacent-square interval; it is an N,k-derived phase coordinate, not additional information.

terminal_caveat: NO_MATERIAL_MATCH_IN_AUDITED_SET is not evidence of novelty, patentability, priority, or algorithmic advantage. It only records that the exact C5 ordering was not located in the frozen audit surfaces/queries.
